paper_metadata.title: Financial Fraud Detection: A Comparative Study of Quantum Machine Learning Models

summary: The paper compares four gate‑based QML models (QSVC, VQC, Estimator QNN, Sampler QNN) on a 200‑sample balanced subset of the BankSim fraud dataset using a 4‑qubit encoding simulated with Qiskit Aer. QSVC with a ZFeatureMap achieved the best performance with F1 ≈ 0.98 for both fraud and non‑fraud classes, followed by VQC with F1 ≈ 0.90 and EQNN with F1 ≈ 0.78, while SQNN achieved ≈0.58 accuracy. All experiments were conducted on a noiseless simulator with no classical baseline comparison.

experiments.description: Comparative fraud-detection experiment on the BankSim dataset using QSVC with three gate-based feature maps (ZZFeatureMap, PauliFeatureMap, ZFeatureMap) and Qiskit/Aer simulation.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features are encoded into quantum states using Qiskit feature maps (ZZFeatureMap, PauliFeatureMap, ZFeatureMap).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of transactions into fraudulent vs non-fraudulent classes.

problem_instance.description: Credit-fraud detection on a balanced subset of the BankSim synthetic bank-payments dataset.

dataset_specification.description: BankSim simulator data; balanced subset with 100 fraudulent and 100 non-fraudulent records; features selected for modeling were age, gender, category, and amount.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Extracted a balanced 200-record subset; converted age categories to integers using regular expressions; label-encoded categorical features (category, gender); removed unused features; split into training and testing sets with train_test_split.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Model evaluated on held-out test set using precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy; results reported for each feature map.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature selection via PCA and logical/correlation analysis; label encoding; train-test split.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classification metrics computed on test set.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: not analyzed; experiment uses 4 qubits simulated with Qiskit Aer
limiting_factors: evaluation performed only on noiseless simulator

notes: num_qubits inferred as 4 because the paper states the selected features are age, gender, category, and amount, and the feature maps are described for four features/qubits.
circuit depth not reported explicitly; feature-map structure is shown but no total depth or transpiled depth is given.
hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states use of the Aer backend with the QasmSimulator.
Paper suggests quantum methods may outperform classical approaches but provides no experimental classical baseline.
Results only compare different QML models.
